newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Iscaycruz says operations back to normal.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Iscaycruz says operations back to normal.

text.p: Operations at Peru's largest zinc miner Iscaycruz S.A. are back to normal after the government provided a permit for a tailings dumping site, a company source said Monday.
The government ordered the miner to halt part of its operations at the beginning of December because the company did not have the right paperwork.
But "now the permit has been obtained so the plant can operate normally," the company source said, adding that the permit was granted on January 6.
Company officials have maintained that production was unaffected by the partial halt in operations, which they did not specify.
Iscaycruz, which is controlled by Switzerland's Glencore Group, started production of zinc concentrates at its 125,000 tonne capacity mine in July.

The Iscaycruz mine - situated more than 4,500 meters (15,000 feet) above sea level in the Andean province of Oyon 100 miles (160 km) northeast of Lima - also has a capacity to produce around 9,000 tonnes annually of lead concentrates.

Iscaycruz expects to exploit for at least seven years its proven and probable mineral reserves of 2.7 million tonnes, which have one of the highest zinc grades in the world at 21.4 percent. The reserves' lead grade is 2.2 percent.
